problem:
Given that 

$$
\frac{2x-5}{(x-5)^{2}}=\frac{2}{x-5}+\frac{B}{(x-5)^{2}},
$$

what is the value of $B?$
worked_solution:
Multiplying both sides of the given equality by $(x-5)^{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-5 & =2(x-5)+B.\end{aligned}
$$

Letting $x=5$  gives

$$
\begin{aligned}2(5)-5 & =2(5-5)+B \\ 10-5 & =2(0)+B \\ 5 & =0+B \\ B & =5.\end{aligned}
$$
